result:
I found 12 rules in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match their docstrings (or the shared rules at the top of the module), and fixed all of them. To check, I wrote a reference version from the docstrings and compared all 150 rules against it over many quantity and price combinations. Before the fix 12 rules differed; afterwards none do. Every rule still raises an error on negative input, and `quote()` works as before.

| Rule | What it did | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | Discount started at 31 units, not 30 | `qty >= 31` → `qty >= 30` |
| 51 | Discount started at 101 units, not 100 | `qty > 100` → `qty >= 100` |
| 27, 41, 80, 136 | The cap was applied to the price before the percentage, instead of to the discount (the module docstring says the discount is capped) | Calculate the discount first, then apply `min(disc, cap)` |
| 46 | Labeled "marginal" but discounted every unit | Discount only the units above the threshold: `(qty - 20) * unit * 8 // 100` |
| 79 | Same problem: "marginal" but discounted every unit | `(qty - 10) * unit * 15 // 100` |
| 65 | Rounded the discount instead of dropping fractions of a won (the docstring says floor) | `round(... / 100)` → `... // 100` |
| 87 | Took 4% instead of the documented 3% | `* 4` → `* 3` |
| 105, 150 | Took 16% instead of the documented 15% | `* 16` → `* 15` |

Prices from these 12 rules will change for some orders. For example, rule 46 at 30 units of 1,000 won used to come to 27,600 won and now comes to 29,200 won. Anything that relied on the old amounts will see different results.

I left the other 138 rules unchanged. Some are written differently from the rest (`100 <= qty`, `not qty < 20`, `(qty * unit) * pct`, `if disc > cap`), but they give the same results the docstrings describe.

There's no git in this folder, so I saved a copy of the original file as `pricebook_orig.py` in the scratchpad.

STATUS: DONE
